verdict.rationale: Microsoft's Copilot documentation lists 'Copilot Chat in Outlook and Teams' and says users can 'interact with Copilot using web data and work data', so a built-in AI assistant exists inside Teams. The evidence never shows what tasks a user can hand off to it or how far it can act on them. The Teams agents platform, toolkit CLI and slash commands are developer building blocks for custom agents, not the built-in assistant, so they earn no credit here. Missing for 10: documentation of concrete task delegation or actions Copilot performs inside Teams (e.g. summarizing meetings, drafting messages, acting on the user's behalf), clarity on whether Copilot is native to Teams or a separate Microsoft 365 add-on, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can delegate tasks to a built-in AI assistant inside the product
